newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syrian playwright Wannous dies of cancer.
newsitem.headline: Syrian playwright Wannous dies of cancer.

text.p: Syrian playwright and intellectual Saadallah Wannous died of cancer on Thursday, two days after he was nominated for the Nobel prize for literature, his family said. He was 56.

The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation (UNESCO) had approved on Tuesday a recommendation by the Damascus Arabic Language Forum to nominate Wannous for the Nobel award, the family said.
They said Wannous would be buried in his home town of Husain al-Bahr on the Syrian coast on Friday.
Wannous achieved fame throughout the Arab world with his plays, especially "An Entertainment Party for June 5", about Israel's defeat of Arabs in the 1967 Middle East war.
His plays were performed in most Arab states and widely translated. His works included "The King is the King", "Life Ever", "A Day of Our Time", and "Tipsy Days".
Wannous graduated from Cairo University in 1963 as a journalist and started his career at the Syrian Ministry of Education, where he translated and wrote several books on drama and culture.
Wannous was asked by UNESCO last year to write the organisation's speech on the International Day of Theatre and became the first Arab writer so honoured.
He had been fighting throat cancer for six years but during that time wrote six plays considered by critics to be among his best works.
